lesson.subtitle: Lesson 29 -- Client Relationships: Building Trust (Present Perfect + For / Since)
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Rafael Gasparelli Lima | Lesson 29 -- Built on Trust
lesson.grammar_point: present perfect with for and since for duration (how long have you...?)

listenings.text: Why do clients stay with the same supplier for many years? It isn't only the price. It's trust. Here are three simple rules. First, be honest. When there's a problem, call the client the same day. Don't wait. Second, keep your promises. If you say Monday, deliver on Monday. A reliable partner doesn't surprise people with bad news at the last minute. Third, stay in contact, even when there's no business to discuss. Ask about the client's team and their plans. I have worked with some of my clients for fifteen years, and I have known one of them since my first job. That's a long-standing relationship. Remember: a contract lasts one year. Trust can last for twenty.

Hello Rafael, this is Daniel Visser from Harbor Fresh. I'm calling about your presentation last Thursday. Our directors were very satisfied. As you know, we have worked with Picunha since 2025, and in that time you have never missed a delivery. I have been at Harbor Fresh for twelve years, and I have seen many suppliers come and go. Not many are as reliable as you. So, we want to offer Picunha a three-year contract, starting in January. Claire will send you the details by email on Friday. Please call me back when you can. Thanks, and talk soon.

extra_audio.text: First, thank the client for the call. Then, remember how long you have worked together. Next, ask about their expectations for next year. After that, be honest about any problem. Finally, make one clear promise and keep it.
